items.title: An absent teacherId passes the ownership check
items.body:
The Teacher branch returns `!resource.teacherId || resource.teacherId === actor.teacherId` for assignment actions. `resource` defaults to `{}`, so `resource.teacherId` is undefined and `!undefined` is true. Ownership is only enforced when the caller passes the owning teacher id.

- *Always false without an owner*: the code does the opposite; the empty case is allowed.
- *Every assignment by design*: a Teacher who passes a different teacherId is refused.
- *Only SchoolManager*: the Teacher branch grants assignment updates directly.

items.title: The Late, unscored submission falls out of the average
items.body:
In `calculateGradeSummary` at this commit, Missing adds its points to `possiblePoints` and continues. Late only increments `lateCount`, then the `typeof score.score === "number"` block is skipped because there is no score. Nothing else runs, so the Late item adds to neither total: 80 / 100 = 80%.

- *40%* is what the later fix produces (Late-unscored counted like Missing); it is not in this code yet.
- *null* would need no possible points at all; the graded 80/100 supplies them.
- *Half credit* is not a rule anywhere in this function.

items.title: No Guardian branch means no permissions
items.body:
`canPerform` checks Admin, SchoolManager, Teacher, Advisor and Student in turn. A Guardian matches none of them and reaches the final `return false`, whatever the action and whatever the resource. The audit's design issue 11 makes the same point.

- *Own notification always allowed*: there is no ownership rule for notifications at this commit.
- *Read-only access*: there is no read branch; the function only answers yes or no per action.
- *Reads allowed, writes denied*: no action, read or write, reaches a true return for this role.

items.title: Terminal approvals cannot move
items.body:
`canTransitionApproval` first checks whether the current status is terminal (Approved, Rejected or Cancelled). Approved is, so the transition is refused with "Completed approval decisions are immutable for auditability." before the target status is even considered.

- *Allowed because Cancelled is terminal*: being a valid target only helps when moving from Requested.
- *Allowed for the approver*: the function takes no actor; there is no such rule.
- *Cancelled only from Draft*: there is no Draft status in this function; Requested is the only non-terminal starting point it accepts.

excerpts.quote: Completed approval decisions are immutable for auditability.

items.title: Agents, confidence penalties and log fingerprints
items.body:
The six agents in `packages/agents/src/` share a shape: build output from domain summaries, compute a confidence, emit findings, recommendations and a trace.

- `helpers.ts` has `confidenceFromSignals(base, penalties)`. In `at-risk-agent.ts`, read the three penalty expressions and the conditions that switch each one on.
- `at-risk-agent.ts` also picks a recommendation owner and priority from the risk level. Compare that expression with the audit's bug 7.
- `packages/application/src/services/agent-run-service.ts` builds every agent's input. Find `buildTeacherWorkloadInput` and read the filter that produces `highRiskStudentCount`.
- `packages/observability/src/index.ts` has `fingerprintLog`. Read both regular expressions carefully, then test the audit's example messages against them by hand.

The audit sections "What Went Well" 9, 11 and 12 and "Bugs" 7 and 8 cover these files.

items.title: An exhausted retry becomes a dead letter
items.body:
`retryJob` sees a Failed job with `attempts >= maxAttempts` and returns `nextStatus: "DeadLettered"`, `allowed: false`. `retryBackgroundJob` only throws when the decision is refused **and** the next status is not DeadLettered, so it falls through, writes DeadLettered (keeping attempts at 3 and the error message), and audits the change as `job.retried`.

- *Throws CONFLICT*: that branch is skipped for the DeadLettered decision.
- *Requeued with attempts 4*: requeueing needs attempts below maxAttempts.
- *Requeued at attempts 3*: the status written is DeadLettered, not Queued.

items.title: Adding up the confidence penalties
items.body:
The at-risk agent calls `confidenceFromSignals(86, [...])` with three penalties: 20 when the grade average is null, 15 when the attendance rate is null, 4 when there are no recent support notes. Here the first and third apply: 86 - 20 - 4 = 62.

- *66* applies only the grade penalty.
- *47* also applies the attendance penalty, but the attendance rate is known.
- *86* applies no penalties at all.

items.title: Critical and High share one owner
items.body:
The recommendation is `recommendation(result.level === "Low" ? "Teacher" : "Advisor", ..., result.level === "Critical" || result.level === "High" ? "high" : "medium")`. For Critical: owner Advisor, priority high.

- *Admin* is the audit's proposed fix, not the current code.
- *Teacher, medium* is the Low-level case for the owner and the Medium/Low case for priority.
- *Advisor, medium* has the right owner but the priority belongs to Medium and Low students.

items.title: Six hex characters are not an id
items.body:
`fingerprintLog` lowercases the message, replaces runs of **eight or more** hex characters with `{id}`, then replaces digit runs with `{n}`. "abc123" is only six characters, so it is not an id; its digits become `{n}`. The messages normalise to "student abc{n} has {n} absences" and "student def{n} has {n} absences", which hash differently. The audit (section 9 of "What Went Well") says they match; the code disagrees.

- *Each id becomes {id}*: true only for ids of 8+ hex characters.
- *Hash covers only service, level and entity*: the normalised message is in the hashed string.
- *Counts keep them apart*: counts become `{n}` in both; the letters are what differ.

items.title: Summing the risk bands
items.body:
`scoreStudentRisk` starts at 10. Average 65 is in the 60-69 band: +25. Two missing assignments: +2 * 4 = 8. Five absences meet the `>= 5` band: +28. Declining: +12. One active intervention: -6. One support note does not exceed 2: nothing. Total 77, and `riskLevelFromScore` maps 60-79 to High.

- *83, Critical* forgets the -6 for the active intervention.
- *71, High* subtracts the intervention penalty twice; it applies once.
- *59, Medium* drops the Declining +12 and subtracts the intervention twice; neither happens.

items.title: Consecutive records, not consecutive days
items.body:
`findLongestAbsenceStreak` sorts by date, then walks the records: each Absent increments the run, anything else resets it. The dates are used only for sorting. Two Absent records with nothing between them form a run of 2, even three weeks apart.

- *1* would need a date-gap check, which this version does not have.
- *0* invents a minimum streak length; the function returns the plain count.
- *Only on school days* describes the later session-aware version, not this one.

items.title: Pure domain functions worth tracing by hand
items.body:
`packages/domain/src/` holds the rules as pure functions with no database. Before the quizzes, trace these on paper:

- `grades.ts`, `calculateGradeSummary`: for each submission status, note which counters and which totals it changes. The audit's bug 6 is about one status in particular.
- `risk.ts`, `scoreStudentRisk` and `riskLevelFromScore`: a base score plus additive bands. Write the band table out (grades, missing work, attendance, trend, interventions, notes) so you can add up an example.
- `attendance.ts`, `findLongestAbsenceStreak`: read what the loop compares and what it ignores.
- `jobs.ts`: `retryJob`, `markDeadLettered` and `calculateNextRetryAt`. Then read how `job-service.ts` acts on each possible decision.
- `approvals.ts` and `permissions.ts`: list the terminal statuses, and list which roles have a branch in `canPerform` and what each branch does when no resource is passed.

The tests in `packages/domain/src/domain.test.ts` pin some of these; predict first, then check.

items.title: Powers of two, floored at 1 and capped at 60
items.body:
`calculateNextRetryAt` computes `Math.min(60, Math.max(1, 2 ** attempts))` minutes and adds them to a copy of `now`. For attempts 0, `2 ** 0` is 1. For attempts 7, `2 ** 7` is 128, clamped to 60.

- *0 and 128* ignores both the floor and the cap.
- *1 and 128* ignores only the cap; the audit names the 60-minute cap explicitly.
- *2 and 64* uses `2 ** (attempts + 1)`, which is not the formula.

items.title: An equality check that drops Critical
items.body:
`buildTeacherWorkloadInput` filters enrolled students by `scoreStudentRisk(...).level === "High"`. Of 2 High, 3 Critical and 10 Low students, only the 2 High ones pass, so the workload agent sees 2 and its "Many high-risk students" signal stays quieter than it should.

- *5* is what the audit recommends the code should count (`High` or `Critical`).
- *3* reverses the comparison.
- *15* ignores the filter; every student is scored, but only matches are counted.

items.title: Start here: the education ops app as its audit found it
items.body:
This repo is the original Agentic Education Operations codebase, before its twenty-story backlog was built (that later state is a separate quest). The pack tests the code as it stands at this commit, guided by the author's own audit.

Read in this order:

1. `docs/05-domain-model-guide.md`: the entities and the business rules in one page.
2. `docs/03-agent-system-guide.md`: what an agent is here (deterministic, offline) and what a run records.
3. `docs/11-codebase-audit-and-review.md`: what went well, what is over-built, and a numbered list of bugs. Most quizzes start from one of its sections.

The audit names files and functions for every claim. Open each one and read the code next to the claim; the quizzes give concrete inputs and ask what the code returns at this commit. The audit is usually right but not always, so when the prose and the code differ, the code decides.

The agent system is fully local, deterministic, and mocked.
